collection.description: For weeks the ground has been cracked and grey.

ask.text:
For weeks the ground has been cracked and grey. The stream shrank to a trickle. The farmers planted anxiously, watered by hand, and watched the sky every evening for clouds that never came.
Then, this afternoon, the sky finally opens.
Children dance in the puddles, shrieking. (Name) and the other farmers stand in the fields with their faces turned up to the rain, laughing like fools, soaked to the skin.
Then the rain does not stop. It gets heavier. And heavier. And from inside the storehouse, whose roof has dried out and gone brittle over the long drought, comes a sound everyone recognizes: drip... drip... drip-drip-drip. The rain is a blessing, but the stores are getting wet, and the paths are turning to mud. What should (name) do first?

choices.label: Mark How Fast the Ground Drinks

c1o1.text: The mats go on just in time, and the quick-thinking villagers in the fields pull the ripe gourds in before the downpour can split them open. The storehouse stays dry, and the rescued gourds add a little food to the stores. (Name) collapses on a bench, soaked and grinning.

text_only.reason: the word in the owner's story; what changes in the game is the ending's own EFFECT line (the ledger), so this word alone changes nothing

c1o2.text: Water gets in under the mats anyway, running in rivulets down the inside walls. By the time anyone notices, a basket of dried fish at the back is soaked through and swimming. It has to be thrown out. After weeks of praying for rain, nobody quite knows how to feel about this.

c1.text: (Name) shouts for help, and a team of soaked villagers races to drag palm mats over the storehouse roof, while others run for the fields...

c2o1.text: Everyone is safe. Families whose roofs are leaking squeeze together in the driest huts to wait out the rain, sharing blankets and stories and complaining cheerfully about each other's feet. It is crowded, damp and surprisingly happy.

c2o2.text: Running back from the far huts, (name) slips on the field path, which has turned from dust into slick mud in an instant, and goes down hard. (His/Her) leg twists under (him/her) badly. (He/She) has to be carried to the healers, and will need their care for a while before (he/she) can walk properly again.

c2.text: (Name) runs through the village, splashing through puddles, checking that everyone is safe and dry...

c3o1.text: By the time the rain finally eases, (name) has noticed a clear pattern: the terraced plots on the slope soaked up the rain like a sponge, while the flat ones by the stream flooded and washed away. It's a useful lesson for next season's planting, and the farmers start building terraces on the flat ground.

c3o2.text: The sticks in different fields disagree completely: one flat field flooded, another didn't; one terrace soaked it up, another ran with mud. The farmers decide to wait for the next rain before guessing at anything. (Name) is very wet and has learned nothing, but (he/she) doesn't seem to mind.

c3.text: While everyone else panics, (name) stands in the rain with a bundle of sticks, pushing them into the ground in different fields to see where the water soaks in and where it pools...

c4o1.text: The workers patch the worst roofs before dark, and the storehouse stays dry through the night. The village goes to sleep to the sound of rain on solid thatch, which, after the long drought, is the most beautiful sound anyone has ever heard.

c4o2.text: The patching goes on and on, right through dinner and into the night. The soaked, shivering, hungry workers have to be fed twice, and it all comes out of the stores, leaving a little less food. Nobody begrudges it.

c4.text: (Name) gathers every pair of hands that isn't busy, and they set to work on the leaking roofs with fresh thatch and sap, in the pouring rain...
